An entry here is a claim that a human looked and the gap is intended. It must say what the
member is for and what, if anything, consumes it - the gate cannot answer the consumer question
itself without false positives, because vocabulary members are short common words (`package`,
`artifact` and `finding` all occur in unrelated enums in this repo).
Both directions ratchet: a NEW gap fails, and so does an entry whose gap has been closed. A
baseline that still claims something no longer true is a false record, which is the thing this

reserved_members.reason: D-F2. Declared in the enum, in the scan_started handshake and in the TypeScript schema, and produced by no extractor. Its only intended consumer is `test_expected_for_changed_module`, whose dispatch is "none" - the kind has no evaluator either - so both halves are absent and neither could be discovered from the other. Kept rather than removed because the pair is a deliberate placeholder for change-coverage enforcement; the honest record is that the engine advertises a fact it cannot emit. Emitting it is what closes this entry.

D-F2. Consumed by candidate_command.rs's `push_guard_candidate` (fact_kind: "csrf_guard_called"), which therefore nominates nothing from it. security_facts.rs has no CSRF guard extractor. The `symbol_called` variant of the same call site still produces api_route_requires_csrf_for_mutation candidates, so the missing kind degrades nomination rather than disabling it - which is why it was invisible.
D-F2, identical in shape to csrf_guard_called: consumed by push_guard_candidate, extracted by nothing, with the `symbol_called` path still covering the kind.

D-G5. Produced by neither the Rust graph builder nor the TypeScript fallback, and consumed by nothing - the string "package" occurs in this repo only as a `specifier_kind` value, an unrelated vocabulary. Reserved for workspace-package nodes, which nothing yet builds.
D-G5. No producer and no consumer; the string "artifact" occurs only as an evidence-surface value elsewhere. Reserved for build-artifact nodes.

D-G5. No producer and no consumer in either language. The import side has `import_decl` and is built; the export side was declared symmetrically and never implemented. Its absence was invisible partly because the dead `GraphNodeRecordSchema` copy named `import` and `role` rather than `import_decl` and `file_role`, so nothing that read a graph vocabulary was reading a correct one.
D-G5. No producer and no consumer. Diagnostics travel as their own stream event and their own table; they were never made graph nodes.

D-G5. No producer. Its intended consumer is the FINDING_HAS_EVIDENCE traversal in packages/query/src/index.ts:688, which walks from a finding node to its evidence - so the traversal exists, the edge kind exists, and neither end of it is ever built. See the FINDING_HAS_EVIDENCE entry.

D-G5, and the sharpest case. packages/query/src/index.ts:688 branches on this edge kind in production code - not a test - to resolve a finding's evidence, and nothing in either language emits it. The query returns empty rather than failing, so the result reads as 'this finding has no evidence' instead of 'this edge is never built'.

Declared in the parser-gap vocabulary and referenced nowhere in either language: no diagnostic maps to it, no capability contract names it, nothing filters on it. Reserved for the reflection case the TypeScript adapter does not attempt.

S2-02. A FINDING-level code (SecurityMissingProofCodeSchema) copied into the PROOF-level enum when the two vocabularies were confused for one - the same confusion that produced S1-01, seen from the other side. `build_session_trust_proof_from_facts` emits only derived_from_request and unknown_helper, so nothing constructs this. RETAINED, not deleted, for stored-row compatibility: SecurityBoundaryProofSchema is applied ON READ in listSecurityBoundaryProofs, so narrowing this enum makes any row already holding the member unparseable, and there is no migration back. scripts/stored-proof-census.mjs reports 18 of 18 databases opened and 0 proof rows on the machine this was written on - an absence of evidence, not evidence of absence, and not a licence to shrink. CONSUMED by phase4_missing_code in check_command.rs, which names it in an explicit arm and passes it through unchanged; it is a member of the finding-level vocabulary too, so that pass-through is correct rather than accidental. Adding a producer closes this entry.

S2-02, and the sharper of the pair. No producer for the same reason as missing_auth_guard, but unlike it this member is NOT in the finding-level vocabulary, so if it were ever emitted the finding would normalize to `unknown_reason_code` at the engine parse boundary and stop saying why the proof failed. It is named explicitly in phase4_missing_code's exhaustive match, pinned by phase4_missing_code_tests, and left unfixed on purpose: choosing a finding-level code for a parser-gapped session-trust proof is a product decision, not a mechanical one - a parser gap travels on the separate parser_gaps surface and drives proof_status == ParserGap, so answering session_not_trusted would assert a trust failure that was never established. Retained for the same stored-row reason as its sibling. If a producer is ever added, decide the finding-level mapping FIRST.
